title: Bank of Canada governor Tiff Macklem to step down in 2027
summary: Bank of Canada governor Tiff Macklem will not seek a second term leading Canada's central bank. His current term as governor will end on June 2, 2027.

image.caption: Tiff Macklem, the governor of the Bank of Canada, will leave his post in 2027. (Ben Nelms/CBC)

blocks.text: Bank of Canada governor Tiff Macklem will not seek a second term leading Canada's central bank. His current term as governor will end on June 2, 2027.
Central bank says it has started search for Macklem's successor
Bank of Canada governor Tiff Macklem will step down from the top job at Canada's central bank when his term expires on June 2, 2027.

In an announcement on Monday, the Bank of Canada said Macklem will not seek a second term as governor when his current seven-year term expires in June. The central bank says it has begun its search for his successor.
"My time as governor has seen Canada navigate a more fragmented, shock-prone world," Macklem, 65, stated on Monday.
"The Bank has faced these challenges by acting decisively, by using sound judgment in the face of uncertainty, and by serving Canadians with humility and a steadfast commitment to its mandate."
Mackelm's retirement was widely expected, as the last time a ​Bank of Canada governor served a second term was ​1980.
During his tenure, Macklem faced unprecedented challenges, including the inflation shock resulting from the COVID-19 pandemic, and the ongoing Canada-U.S. trade war.

Jeff Lagerquist is a senior writer with CBC News based in Toronto. Originally from Erin, Ont., he studied journalism at Toronto Metropolitan University. Jeff previously worked as a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance Canada. He was also a reporter and digital producer for CTV National News, BNN Bloomberg and The Financial Post. In 2025, he was a Columbia University energy journalism fellow.
